claims.text: A controlled heat treatment can induce ordered nanoprecipitates in a refractory high-entropy alloy matrix.
Appropriate control of heat-treatment temperature, time, and cooling rate can favor nucleation of fine, coherent precipitates.
The heat treatment can avoid excessive grain growth and the formation of incoherent, brittle phases.
The intervention will produce a fine, uniform dispersion of coherent nanoprecipitates within the alloy matrix.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength.
The coherent and uniform nature of the nanoprecipitates permits significant dislocation bypass and accumulation.
Dislocation bypass and accumulation enhance work hardening and ductility.
The heat-treated alloy will have a statistically significant increase in yield strength relative to the untreated baseline alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will have a statistically significant increase in uniform elongation relative to the untreated baseline alloy.
The beneficial response depends on the alloy composition supporting coherent-precipitate formation under the selected heat treatment.
Alloys that do not form the targeted coherent precipitates may not show the proposed strength–plasticity improvement.
Formation of incoherent, brittle phases may prevent the proposed strength–plasticity improvement.
